AB Foods Revenue Rises Despite Continued Sugar Price Pressure
By Aimee Look
Associated British Foods reported a rise in revenue for the full fiscal year, but expects its sugar business to continue weighing on results.
The U.K. conglomerate booked 19.58 billion pounds in revenue ($26.25 billion) compared with 19.46 billion pounds a year earlier.
However, many other headlines were in the red, with pretax profit falling 10% to 1.28 billion pounds for the year.

The sugar-to-shirts conglomerate is in the process of splitting its fast-fashion arm Primark from its food units, with completion expected by December 2027. Its foods business--encompassing ingredients, sugar, agriculture and grocery--has traditionally been less favored by investors than the retail business.
For its retail business, which houses the Primark brand, AB Foods said sales rose 2% to 9.8 billion pounds for the year.

The sugar business posted an adjusted operating loss of 47 million pounds in the fiscal year, linked to lower average selling prices in Europe. The loss is expected to deepen to a range of 70 million pounds to 170 million pounds for the following year.
